name: Chen Wei
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Shenzhen Oriental Fortune Capital (东方富海); chairman of the Shenzhen Venture Capital Association
profile: Chen Wei (陈玮), a Xiamen University accounting PhD and former university lecturer, spent about seven years at Shenzhen Capital Group (rising to president) before founding Oriental Fortune Capital in 2006. The VC firm now manages close to RMB 40bn and has backed 600+ companies (e.g. Kunlun Tech, Jiuxian.com). He remains chairman and an active industry spokesman.
interesting_fact: When the 2008 crisis led LPs to cancel staged commitments, Oriental Fortune's first fund shrank from RMB 900m to under RMB 350m; Chen says he personally borrowed RMB 80m to keep the firm going.
deep_cut_fact: He came to venture capital by accident: in 1999, aged 35 and just back from a visiting-scholar stint in the Netherlands, he wanted to join the Shenzhen Stock Exchange, but the ChiNext board was delayed and hiring frozen, so he applied to Shenzhen Capital instead.
notes: Source of wealth 'Oriental Fortune' = Oriental Fortune Capital (东方富海), not Eastmoney (东方财富). Very public VC figure; frequent speaker at Chinese VC forums. No published press email found; the company website did not load from here. Best route: the firm's official channels.

name: Chai Huijing
profile: Chai Huijing (柴慧京) appeared on the Hurun China Rich List from 2008 to 2018 with real-estate wealth tied to a company listed as 'Guodu' (国都). I could not find any public profile, company page or press coverage to confirm her role or what she is doing now.
notes: Very low public footprint; searches for the exact Chinese name returned nothing relevant. Not the Taiwanese general Chai Hui-chen (柴惠珍). Verify via Chinese corporate registries (Qichacha/Tianyancha) before outreach.

name: Steve Parkin
current_role: Founder and former executive chairman of Clipper Logistics (sold to GXO in 2022); private investor through Knaresborough Investments
profile: Leeds entrepreneur who left school at 16 and founded Clipper Group in 1992. He built it into a listed e-commerce and retail logistics firm (LSE IPO 2014) serving retailers such as John Lewis. GXO Logistics bought Clipper for about £965m in 2022, netting Parkin over £100m in cash plus GXO shares. He now invests privately in Yorkshire businesses.
interesting_fact: Clipper began in 1992 with a single van delivering clothing to fashion stores. Thirty years later it sold for roughly £965m.
deep_cut_fact: In 2017 his private-equity vehicle Knaresborough Investments took a 25% stake in a small Leeds electric-heating business. He likened it to Clipper in its early days.
notes: Not to be confused with David Parkin (Yorkshire business journalist with a Substack). Clipper was a Leeds United sponsor and Parkin is a known Leeds fan. He is also reported to own racehorses, but I could not open a source to confirm it. No published personal or office contact found; Clipper is now part of GXO, so its press office is no longer relevant. Best route is probably Yorkshire business networks.

name: Qian Yunbao
profile: Qian Yunbao (钱云宝) was the controlling shareholder of Hengbao Co. (恒宝股份, SZSE 002104), a smart-card maker in Danyang, Jiangsu, and chairman of Jiangsu Hengshen (carbon fibre). A June 2017 Shenzhen Stock Exchange disclosure records his death on 12 April 2017 and the transfer of his shareholdings by inheritance.
notes: Deceased. Source: Hengbao equity-change report filed with the SZSE, 23 June 2017 (https://disc.static.szse.cn/disc/disk01/finalpage/2017-06-23/2d9ddce9-51ba-4b87-b463-e675958b7fe0.PDF). Not an outreach candidate.

name: Sheng Faqiang
current_role: Co-founder and former chairman, Toread Holdings (探路者); no current executive role found
profile: Sheng Faqiang (盛发强) co-founded Beijing outdoor-gear brand Toread in 1999. In 2009 it listed on ChiNext, where it was called the 'first outdoor stock', and he served as chairman during its mid-2010s diversification. In 2021 the founders transferred control to an investor group led by chip-industry executive Li Ming, and Sheng stepped down as chairman.
interesting_fact: Toread was one of the first companies on Shenzhen's ChiNext growth board when it launched in 2009, and was dubbed China's 'first outdoor stock'.
deep_cut_fact: Before outdoor gear he was in printing: around 1993 he quit a state railway survey-and-design institute, worked as a salesman for a printing plant in Beihai, Guangxi, and then set up his own small printing company.
notes: Since 2021 Toread has been controlled by Li Ming's group, so the company website is no longer a direct route to Sheng. Low recent public profile; I found no personal channels.
